title: A Martyr's Bullet
tagline: One shot. One act of defiance. An entire nation's will made visible.

scenes.text: Harbin railway station, Manchuria, October 26, 1909. Korean independence activist Ahn Jung-geun waits on the platform. Japan's most powerful statesman — Itō Hirobumi, the architect of Korea's annexation — is about to step from the train.

scenes.speaker: Itō Hirobumi
scenes.text: Japan brings civilization to Korea — modern law, railways, schools. History will judge this as progress. The old feudal order could not last. Someone would come. We came first.

scenes.speaker: Ahn Jung-geun
scenes.text: I am not a criminal. I am a soldier of the Korean resistance. I have listed fifteen crimes against Itō before God and history. He knows what he has done. So do I.

challenge.instruction: Ahn has ridden the Chinese Eastern Railway from Vladivostok to be waiting when Itō's train arrives. Lay the line from Harbin to Vladivostok, station by station.
challenge.fact: On October 26, 1909, An Jung-geun shot Itō Hirobumi — Japan's first Prime Minister and the architect of Korean colonisation — at Harbin railway station. An was captured, tried, and executed in 1910, the same year Japan formally annexed Korea.

scenes.text: Ahn Jung-geun spent his final weeks writing treatises on Asian peace and human dignity. He was executed in 1910 — the same year Japan formally annexed Korea. He is still regarded as a national hero in Korea and China.

challenge.instruction: Ahn told his judges he was an officer of the Korean Righteous Army, not a murderer. Lead the resistance across the board and capture the enemy pieces.
challenge.fact: An Jung-geun saw himself not as an assassin but as a soldier of justice — his act of resistance at Harbin Station became a symbol of Korean defiance against colonization.

scenes.speaker: Ahn Jung-geun
scenes.text: I dream not of revenge, but of East Asia standing together: Korea, China, Japan — in true partnership. The bullets of empire produce only more empire. But I had no other weapon left.

challenge.instruction: To answer Itō, Ahn had to understand his world. Fill in the words of Meiji Japan and the peninsula it claimed.
challenge.fact: An Jung-geun wrote a treatise on peace in East Asia while awaiting execution, calling for cooperation between China, Japan, and Korea against Western colonialism. He was a complex figure — a Catholic, a scholar, and a revolutionary.

Ahn Jung-geun was executed by Japan in 1910. In Korea he is a national hero; in China, a statue stands at Harbin station where the assassination occurred. In Japan he is officially considered a criminal. The same act reads entirely differently across national histories.
challenge.instruction: Two nations wire two verdicts on the same man. Read the lamp and spell out how the news from Harbin was told.

scenes.speaker: An Jung-geun
scenes.text: This time the whole board is judged at once. Deploy Gregor Mendel, Tenzing Norgay and me, turn us public, then declare the Pilgrimage: the highest public Belief on the board when the round ends takes the prize.

challenge.instruction: Fight lesson 6 · Global Competition. Deploy your Great People, Toggle Public on each, then start the Pilgrimage and End Turn to win the round with the highest public Belief on the board.
challenge.fact: A Global Competition counts every public Great Person on the whole board; followers and face-down cards add nothing. It lasts one round, and the strongest player draws a reward: event cards, followers or a new Great Person.
